notes: This contract pins the bounded embedded IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ restore control path to the official Requirements Lab surfaces. It covers request success/failure, federation-begun and initiate callbacks, complete/not-complete/abort, status response, and in-memory snapshot rollback. The Request Federation Restore report lane additionally pins the one official C++ request declaration and its accepted type-53 label record before the confirmation callback, without extending generic failure reporting. The Federate Restore Complete report lane pins both C++ selectors to §4.31's one type-6 Federate restore-success indicator record before the respective Federation Restored or Federation Not Restored callback, including monotonic report serials across the restored application snapshot. Focused cases restore pre-save live interaction and attribute payloads plus retraction ledgers after post-save Retract terminalized those records, retain saved terminal interaction, timestamped-attribute, and timestamped-object-deletion tombstones as MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted classifications, return saved logical-time and actual-lookahead state after post-save mutations, retain one deferred lookahead-decrease target through restore, reconstitute one process-local single-federate Non-Regulated-Grant pending TAR in both callback models, reconstitute one process-local single-member pending FQR in both callback models, and reconstitute single-federate TARA/NMR/NMRA requests in both callback models. A new three-member case restores one queued timestamped attribute passel for two constrained recipients, proves separate Flush Queue delivery for each, and routes Request Retraction to both delivered recipients. Timed companions retain timestamp-eight default-source attribute and interaction passels across a timestamp-six save boundary, restore them, and prove FQR delivery plus Request Retraction; RL-141 records the cross-service boundary relation. Every fresh grant follows Federation Restored; under HLA_IMMEDIATE it completes before Federate Restore Complete returns. Queued/in-transit TSO beyond these bounded cases, general timed restore, distributed transport, durable external persistence, handle remapping, service-wide interlocks, protected review, package support, and conformance remain open.
